title: Chef John's Loco Moco
description: This loco moco is Chef John's version of Hawaiian comfort food made with a juicy burger patty covered in gravy, topped with a fried egg over rice.
ingredients: 1 pinch salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
2 drops sesame oil, or to taste
2 tablespoons minced green onions, white and light green parts only

steps.text: Season patties with salt, pepper, and cayenne; set aside.
Whisk together beef stock, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, cornstarch, ketchup, sugar, and sesame oil in a bowl; set aside.

Melt 1 teaspoon butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook patties in the hot skillet until the bottoms are nicely browned, about 5 minutes. Flip patties; add green onions and cook until both beef and onions are browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Remove patties and most of green onions to a plate.
Pour beef stock mixture into the skillet. Stir, scraping up browned bits from the bottom, until thickened, about 2 minutes. Reduce heat to low and reserve gravy until needed.
Melt remaining butter in another skillet over medium heat. Add eggs to the skillet and fry side-by-side until whites are set and yolks are still runny.
Divide rice between 2 serving bowls. Place patties over rice, spoon gravy on top, and add fried eggs.

video.description: Is there anything better than a juicy beef patty smothered in even beefier gravy, topped with an oozing fried egg, and served over hot rice? The answer is no; what's more is that it's cheap and quick too! The Hawaiians have got it figured out with this classic comfort food known as loco moco, originally designed for broke, starving college students. You'll start by pre-mixing the gravy ingredients - a savory blend of beef stock, soy sauce, and Worcestershire. Simply pan-fry your beef patties until they develop a nice crust. You'll want to reduce the gravy in those yummy browned bits - thanks to cornstarch, it's quicker than conventional gravies. All that's left is to ready a bed of rice, fry an egg, and load everything into a big, comforting bowl of goodness. Get the recipe for [Chef John's Loco Moco](https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/272767/chef-johns-loco-moco/).
